run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:44:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate (warning) alert is firing because frontend-proxy in namespace otel-demo is returning a small but persistent nonzero rate of HTTP 503 responses. Span metrics show frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans labeled STATUS_CODE_ERROR (~1-6 error spans per 5 min from ~18:21 through 19:02, error ratio <=0.0014 of ingress spans), and sampled traces at 18:34-18:39 pair those 503 ingress spans with a 'router frontend egress' child span carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0", with no frontend-service span in the same trace. frontend-proxy access logs name the exact failure: "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" for the upstream cluster "frontend" (e.g. GET /, GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO, GET /api/data/?contextKeys=travel), interleaved with normal 200 responses. The frontend pod itself never restarted (0 restarts, running since 18:05:45), has no error-status spans, and its Service has one ready endpoint (100.96.4.88:8080), so a crash or endpoint removal is not the explanation; however the frontend container runs pinned at its 100m CPU limit (~0.10-0.11 cores) with the highest CFS throttling ratio in the namespace (0.27-0.38 of periods) and its sampled request spans take 0.7-1.0 s (e.g. 748,090 us client span for ProductCatalogService/GetProduct vs a 128 us product-catalog server span). The remaining reason the frontend terminates connections before responding is not proven: Envoy config is not exposed in any otel-demo ConfigMap and the frontend container produced no readable log lines. A separate incident at the same time - fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 18:44:43 and chaos-mesh PodNetworkChaos resources on both fraud-detection pods and kafka were being updated every minute from 18:42:40 - is not connected to the frontend-proxy 503s (the failing traces contain only load-generator -> frontend-proxy -> frontend-egress spans). The alert rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus, so the reported alert value 0.0111 could not be reproduced from the span metrics.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span metrics for the query window carry the status labels STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so error-status spans exist for this service.

A 72-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"} evaluated at 18:56:41 and 19:01:41 returned 14.28 and 15.21 error-status 'ingress' spans against 25,831 and 27,090 non-error 'ingress' spans; the 'router frontend egress' span had zero error-status spans (its failures are tagged error=true with http.status_code=0, not otel ERROR).

Per-minute 5-minute increases of frontend-proxy 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans stayed between 0 and 5.56 from 18:21 to 19:02; the trace-metric series starts around 18:21, so no earlier error-rate baseline exists in this data.

The ratio of error to total frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans computed from 5-minute rates ranged from 0 up to 0.00142 (0.142%) between 18:35 and 19:01; this observed span-based ratio does not reproduce the alert annotation's 0.0111.

Sampled failing traces show frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with error=true, http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR, their child 'router frontend egress' spans with error="true" and http.status_code="0", and the corresponding load-generator 'GET' spans with http.status_code=503 and error=true; the same traces contain no frontend-service span.

Whole trace 006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c (18:38:02Z) contains exactly four spans: load-generator user_browse_product, load-generator GET (503, error), frontend-proxy ingress (503, error) and frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error, http.status_code 0); no frontend span and no downstream service spans are present.

frontend-proxy access logs contain the exact failure text "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" for the upstream cluster "frontend", e.g. "GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO" (18:38:02.248Z), "GET /" (18:38:02.281Z) and "GET /api/products/1YMWWN1N4O" (18:38:50.712Z), interleaved with 200 via_upstream responses from the same upstream.
The same 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} pattern with upstream cluster "frontend" is still present at 18:54:35Z for "GET /api/data/?contextKeys=travel".

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t (IP 100.96.4.88) and frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq (IP 100.96.4.190) are both Running, all pod conditions are True, restartCount is 0, and the frontend container has been running since 18:05:45Z; the frontend container limits are cpu 100m / memory 200Mi and the frontend-proxy container limits are cpu 30m / memory 50Mi.

The frontend Service selects opentelemetry.io/name=frontend on port 8080 (targetPort 8080) and its Endpoints object has exactly one ready address, 100.96.4.88:8080, pointing at pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t, so frontend-proxy's upstream target exists and is Ready.

frontend span metrics for 18:40-19:00 contain no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series: GET, POST, the /api routes, /api/products/{productId}, /api/recommendations and all frontend gRPC client operations are reported with STATUS_CODE_UNSET only, and the frontend handled roughly 4,500-5,500 GET spans and 1,300-1,400 POST spans per 10 minutes.

Across the namespace, only frontend-proxy 'ingress' (11.2) had request-level error spans in the 30 minutes to 19:00; the other nonzero error series are flagd EventStream streaming spans in fraud-detection (5.09), ad (3.05) and recommendation (2.04), while frontend, checkout, payment, accounting and the other services' request spans return 0 in that same metric.

The frontend container consumed about 0.100-0.113 CPU cores against its 100m limit and was CFS-throttled in 0.27-0.38 of periods every minute from 18:20 to 18:59, while frontend-proxy consumed about 0.028 cores against its 30m limit and was throttled in 0.05-0.08 of periods.

At 19:00 the frontend pod had the highest CFS throttling ratio in otel-demo (0.353), above product-catalog (0.226), postgresql (0.216), cart (0.199), quote (0.195), fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b (0.176) and ad (0.174).

Working-set memory of the frontend container was 125-128 MB against its 200Mi limit and frontend-proxy was about 20 MB against its 50Mi limit over 18:30-19:00, so neither container was memory-saturated.

Sampled frontend request spans are slow: GET /api/data 953,489 us, GET /api/products/{productId} 802,746 us and 754,501 us, GET /api/recommendations 706,983 us, POST /api/checkout 925,718 us; in trace b166da27ff3ef1a1df414050cc7e4abb the frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct lasted 748,090 us while the matching product-catalog server span lasted 128 us.
All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure = False; no node resource-pressure condition was observed.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst restarted at 18:44:43Z: its container's lastState shows terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, restartCount 1, and it is Ready now; its sibling fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b has restartCount 0. This is a separate change on a different service from the frontend-proxy alert.

Kubernetes events retained for 18:42:40-18:54:40Z show chaos-mesh PodNetworkChaos resources named fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9 receiving 'Updated' events every minute, plus Created/Pulled/Started events for pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst at 18:44:43Z; within that returned event set no frontend-related PodNetworkChaos event appears.

The otel-demo ConfigMaps are flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products; there is no frontend-proxy Envoy configuration ConfigMap in that namespace, so the proxy's upstream timeouts, keepalive and retry settings could not be inspected.

Counter to a frontend crash, OOM kill or endpoint removal as the cause of the 503s: the frontend container has 0 restarts and no previous instance, all pod conditions are True, its Service has a ready endpoint, and its span metrics contain no error-status spans while it continues to serve thousands of requests per 10 minutes; the failures are therefore connection terminations, not process restarts.

Most likely mechanism supported by the evidence: the frontend container is running at its 100m CPU limit with the namespace's highest CFS throttling ratio (0.27-0.38), and under that starvation some accepted frontend connections are terminated before a response starts, which frontend-proxy reports as 503 with response flag UC and which leaves no frontend span; this is a mechanism hypothesis, not a proven cause, because no frontend log line or app-level error was observable.

Remaining candidate that the data cannot exclude: a connection-reuse / keepalive race between the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream pool and the Node.js frontend server, where the frontend closes a pooled connection just as a request is dispatched. Some failures are near-instant (8 ms and 51 ms) which fits this pattern, but Envoy's upstream idle/timeout settings are not readable, so it cannot be confirmed or rejected.

Remaining candidate: saturation of frontend-proxy's own very small CPU limit (30m; ~0.028 cores used, 0.05-0.08 throttled periods) could add handling delay to proxied requests. It is recorded as a candidate only; the UC response flag attributes termination to the upstream side, so this cannot by itself explain the 503s.

Rejected: the fraud-detection OOMKill (18:44:43Z) and the chaos-mesh PodNetworkChaos updates on fraud-detection/kafka pods explain the frontend-proxy 503s. The failing traces contain only load-generator -> frontend-proxy ingress -> frontend egress spans with no checkout, fraud-detection or kafka span; the failed requests are index/product/data routes; the proxy's named upstream is "frontend"; and the frontend's sampled CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client spans report rpc.grpc.status_code=0. The near-coincidence with the alert start (18:44:41 vs 18:44:43) is not causation, and the proxy error spans already exist from ~18:21.

Read the actual RequestErrorRate rule (Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source) to confirm its metric, window and threshold: no rules are loaded in this Prometheus, and the span-based error ratio (max 0.00142) does not reproduce the alert annotation's 0.0111.

Review and raise the frontend Deployment's CPU limit (currently 100m while usage sits at 0.100-0.113 cores and 27-38% of CFS periods are throttled), then re-check the 503 UC rate at frontend-proxy; also review the frontend-proxy 30m CPU limit.

Obtain the frontend-proxy Envoy bootstrap/route configuration (it is not in an otel-demo ConfigMap) and check upstream idle_timeout, keepalive settings and retry policy, since 503 UC from upstream connection termination is normally retriable.

Verify/repair frontend container log collection (no lines were readable for its whole lifetime) and review the chaos-mesh experiment scope so injected faults on fraud-detection and kafka are not confused with application faults.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting/recording rule is not present in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no rule groups), so the alert's exact metric, window and threshold are unknown and its reported value 0.0111 could not be reproduced from the span metrics.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 18:05:43-19:02:09Z (0 bytes read for the current and previous instances), so any application-level error behind the connection terminations is unknown.
No frontend-proxy Envoy configuration exists in the otel-demo ConfigMaps; upstream idle/keepalive timeouts, circuit breakers and retry policy could not be verified.

chaos-mesh custom resources (PodNetworkChaos/NetworkChaos) are not queryable with the permitted resource kinds; only their 'Updated' events were visible, so whether any chaos experiment also targets the frontend pod is unknown.

Node-level CPU and load metrics (node_cpu_seconds_total, node_load*) are not present in this Prometheus, so CPU contention on node i-029c97e90b3730286, which hosts frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator, ad, cart, checkout, currency, product-catalog and fraud-detection-xdwst, could not be assessed.

No comparable baseline exists for the error rate or latency: the traces_span_metrics series for frontend-proxy begins around 18:21 and Jaeger retains only recent traces, so no latency or error-rate trend can be asserted, only values inside the observed window.

Searches for frontend spans tagged error=true and for frontend-proxy spans with http.status_code=504 returned no data (not proof of absence), so the absence of frontend-tagged errors and of 504 timeouts is unconfirmed.
The retained Kubernetes event range covers only 18:42:40-18:54:40Z; earlier events, including any chaos activity before 18:42:40 or events for frontend objects, are unavailable.
next_steps: Fetch the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source used to fire this alert and confirm whether its 0.0111 value comes from a metric other than traces_span_metrics_calls_total.
Inspect the frontend Deployment/pod CPU limit (100m) against observed demand and consider raising it; then compare the 503 UC rate before and after.
Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy configuration outside otel-demo ConfigMaps (bootstrap args, mounted config, or image default) for upstream idle_timeout, keepalive and retry_on settings.

Restore/verify frontend application logging so the request-level reason for connection termination can be read, and check whether the frontend's HTTP server keepalive/headers timeout is shorter than the proxy's connection reuse window.

Review chaos-mesh experiments active on 2026-11-16 (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst, kafka-ff7884766-29vm9) to confirm their intended scope and to rule in/out a target on frontend.

view.span_groups_note: span_groups summarizes the spans shown in content; spans the adapter sampled out are not counted in any group.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

notes: Container frontend-proxy has no previous instance (HTTP 400: previous terminated container "frontend-proxy" in pod "frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq" not found); the other streams are unaffected.
view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | {name: .metadata.name, keys: (.data | keys)}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null).
